1.
Heard Sri Vijay Shantam, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

2. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Satyapal Singh, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.159 of 2022, under Sections 323, 498-A, 304-B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Atrauli, District Aligarh.
3. This is a second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected vide order dated 12.7.2023 passed by this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.30251 of 2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that fresh and new ground in the present matter is that as of now the statement of Om Prakash, an uncle of the deceased has been recorded as P.W.3 before the trial court who has not supported the prosecution case and has been declared hostile, para 12 and annexure 10 and 11 of the affidavit has been placed before the Court.

It is argued that looking to the said fact and further the fact that earlier two witnesses have also been declared hostile and have not supported the prosecution case, the present case is a fit case where the applicant be enlarged on bail.
It is further submitted that the testimony of all the witnesses has been recorded and statement of one formal witness is pending, as such appropriate direction be passed for expediting the trial.
It has also been pointed out that the applicant is not having any criminal history as stated in para 16 of the affidavit and is in jail since 29.4.2022.

5. Per contra learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the first bail of the applicant was rejected by this Court on merits by a detailed order vide order dated 12.7.2023.

In so far as the hostility of witnesses is concerned, the Court while rejecting the first bail application had considered the fact that two prosecution witnesses have turned hostile and as such there is no substantial change in situation and circumstances.
The bail application be thus rejected.
6. After hearing the counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that this is a second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 12.7.2023.
The said order is extracted hereunder:-
" 1 . List revised.

2. Heard Sri S.K. Verma, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ram Prakash Shukla,
learned A.G.A. and perused the material on record.
3.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Satyapal Singh, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in Session Trial No. 1929 of 2022, Case Crime No. 159 of 2022, under Sections 498A,
323, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Atrauli, District Aligarh.

4. The First Information Report was lodged by Ratiram against the applicant Satyapal Singh, Bani Singh and Dinesh Devi alleging therein that his niece Bharti Devi was married to the applicant around 1-1/2 years back.
There was demand of additional dowry of Rs.1 lakh and motorcycle by the accused persons.
Despite various discussions they did not letup their demand.

On 26.4.2023 at about 10.00 A.M.
Bharti Devi was done to death by all accused persons.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that although the applicant is husband of the deceased but he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the deceased committed suicide and died.

It is further argued that the trial in the present matter has started in which the first informant has been examined as P.W.-1,
copy of the same has been placed before the Court which is annexure no. 8 to the Satyapal Singh vs State Of U.P. on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181028095/
2 affidavit.

entities.text: Satyapal Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that in the cross examination the said witness has stated that no statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded.
It is argued that the said witness has stated that the deceased was of intemperate in nature.
Further it is argued that the mother of the deceased was examined before the trial court as P.W.-2 who did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.
It is argued that as such implication of the applicant is false.

The applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para 12 and is in jail since 29.4.2022.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and argued that in so far as the deceased is concerned, she at the time of incident, was found to be having gravid uterus with a 2-1/2 to 3 months fetus.

It is further argued that although the deceased was found to have ligature mark on her body and cause of death has been opined as asphyxia due to ante mortem hanging but commission of suicide at the stage of pregnancy by a woman is unnatural.

Further it is argued that the first informant while being examined in court has supported the prosecution case in examination-in-chief and even subsequently P.W.-2 the mother of the deceased did not support the prosecution case and has been declared hostile the same can be appreciated by the trial court at the appropriate stage and therefore, the present bail application be rejected.
7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased died in her matrimonial house after about 1-1/2 years of marriage.
She was found to have a gravid uterus with a 2-1/2 to 3 months fetus.
The first informant has supported the prosecution case in examination-in-chief.
8. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected."

7. The ground in the present bail application is that another eye-witness P.W.3 Om Prakash has been examined who has not supported the prosecution case and has been declared hostile, the same does not appear to be a fit ground for enlarging the applicant on bail since the hostility of two witnesses was considered earlier by this Court but still the bail application was rejected.
8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case for bail, hence, the bail application is rejected.

9. However, it is provided that the applicant may file an application for expeditious disposal of the trial of the case before the court concerned within two weeks from today, which may as per its load of work, diary and pendency of cases, pass appropriate orders on the same.

(Samit Gopal, J.) Order Date :- 6.12.2024 Gaurav Kuls  Satyapal Singh vs State Of U.P. on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181028095/
